title: Pete Brown and the all-night jam sessions
summary: Asked what Pete Brown sounded like, Leeman can only say he was wonderful; drummers wore out in the long jams so he was called to fill in.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, before we leave, I'd like to have you mention something about Pete Brown. What kind of a player was he? Mention some of these and describe some of these great musicians that you played with.
Well, as I digested the music and the new music later on, I recorded with Pete and with these people.
But what kind of player was he, Cliff?
He was wonderful. I'm trying to explain -- I couldn't put my finger on it then, but all those musicians were great, and he was one outstanding among many -- but how am I going to compare him?
I'm not asking you to compare him, I just wondered how he sounded.

He was wonderful. Everybody up there was wonderful, everybody on the stand at these clubs. Everybody from the theatre would come by and they'd jam -- they'd do one and two hour sets, the drum men would wear out.
